Code, data & release status → Abstract Overview Data collection Results Citation 01 · Motivation Abstract Dexterous Manipulation Benchmark Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior. Primary area: applications to robotics, autonomy, planning. 02 · Benchmark design Skills and sequences in a shared physical setting. Ten complete tasks and thirty matched stage environments connect household, laboratory and industrial interactions. title: Evaluation — DexArena
text: Evaluation protocol Evaluation Three levels. One physical contract. DexArena separates failures in execution, generalization, and composition while preserving matching task definitions. 01 Stage level Skill execution Run each of the 30 canonical stage environments with its registered robot, horizon, action layout, and physical success predicate. Success rate across fixed seeds Persistent success, not transient contact 29-D single-arm or 58-D bimanual actions 02 Scene level Visual generalization Evaluate every stage on three native scene surfaces using identical object placement and the fixed 256 × 256 policy camera rig. 90 task × scene combinations Shared seeds across algorithms Saved background manifest 03 Sequence level Skill composition Execute two to five dependent stages in their parent long-horizon environment and report complete-sequence success. Stage progress and terminal success Inherited state between stages Single-arm and bimanual tasks Metric contract Report the failure mode, not only the final number. Stage Success Rate Fraction of evaluation episodes whose stage predicate is satisfied for its required hold duration. Cross-scene Average Mean stage success over robocasa_l3_s2, robocasa_l3_s1, and robocasa_l3_s6 with matched seeds. Generalization Gap Difference between the reference collection workspace and native-scene performance. Composition Rate Fraction of complete long-horizon episodes reaching the final task success state. Paper protocol Fifty episodes. Three distinct questions. All six baselines use image observations and robot proprioception, with matched task horizons, randomization and embodiments. Stage and long-horizon success are measured over 50 episodes per task; generalization uses 50 episodes in each of three held-out kitchens without further adaptation. 01 Recorded evaluation seeds The manuscript specifies stage seeds 50000–50049 for ACT and DP. text: Docs / Data & replay Data & replay The release contains 100 replay-successful demonstrations for each of 30 canonical stage tasks. 3,000 episodes 9.1 h teleoperation 20 Hz recording 100 per stage Two-stage review Episodes first enter a pending store with a reviewable MP4. Interactive or success-based review then exports accepted episodes to per-hand LeRobot directories. Frame schema Feature Meaning observation.state Robot proprioception and task state. action Absolute arm and hand joint targets. observation.environment_state Flat environment state for restoration and re-rendering. next.success Per-step result from the environment success predicate. episode.seed Seed used for exact reset and replay. Validation Accepted data is restored in a fresh simulator, rendered offline, and replayed open-loop from the recorded initial state. Only replay-successful trajectories enter the release set. Data collection pipeline VR and glove inputs are converted into joint targets. Recording, review, export and replay validation connect human demonstration collection to offline multi-view rendering. text: DexArena: A Unified Benchmark for Long-Horizon Dexterous Manipulation Author Haonan Ping 1 , Jianshu Hu 2 , Yimin Wang 1 , Yi Zhu 3 , Pai Liang 4 , Qiyan Jin 5 , Qirui Bao 2 , Ying Qian 6 , Xinyang Ding 2 , Hongfei Qiao 2 , Tianle Xue 2 , Yucheng Bai 2 , Soo Wei Jie 2 , Shuguang Li 7 , Yutong Ban 2 Affiliations Submitted 11 September 2026 Last modified 6 October 2026 Status ICLR 2027 Conference Submission · Under review Report Download PDF ↗ OpenReview · #13718 ↗ BibTeX ↓ Repository Code & data release status → Leaderboard View benchmark results → Institute Shanghai Institute for Physical Artificial Intelligence and Robotics · PAIR Community WeChat official account ↗ gh_6279469803d5 Copy ID License CC BY 4.0 ↗ Revisions View on OpenReview ↗ Share Copy paper link Research preview. This is an under-review submission, not an accepted publication. The PDF is the supplied local manuscript snapshot; the modification date above describes the OpenReview record. Code, data & release status → Abstract Overview Data collection Results Citation 01 · Motivation Abstract Dexterous Manipulation Benchmark Long-horizon dexterous manipulation remains a fundamental challenge for robot learning, requiring the composition of multiple skills, precise bimanual coordination, generalizable visual understanding, and robust skill transitions. Yet existing manipulation benchmarks largely emphasize isolated skills or support only a limited range of end-effectors, making these capabilities difficult to evaluate systematically. We introduce DexArena, a benchmark designed to evaluate learning and generalization in long-horizon bimanual dexterous manipulation. DexArena features 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks spanning diverse household and industrial scenarios. Each long-horizon task is composed of explicitly defined stages with physically grounded success conditions, enabling reliable evaluation of both intermediate progress and end-to-end task completion. A unified benchmark interface and verified human-teleoperated demonstrations enable testing different policy learning algorithms, with standardized simulation configurations, scene randomization, trajectory replay, and task-level evaluation. Through extensive baseline experiments, we identify substantial challenges in precise manipulation, generalization to scene variation, and skill composition. DexArena establishes a challenging and reproducible benchmark for developing robot learning methods that move toward generalizable long-horizon dexterous behavior. Primary area: applications to robotics, autonomy, planning. 02 · Benchmark design Skills and sequences in a shared physical setting. Ten complete tasks and thirty matched stage environments connect household, laboratory and industrial interactions. Persistent physical predicates measure both intermediate progress and complete behavior. Figure 1 · DexArena overview. Multi-stage tasks, diverse scenarios, teleoperated demonstrations and multiple embodiments. Full resolution ↗ 03 · Demonstrations From human motion to replayable demonstrations. VR wrist tracking and glove inputs are mapped into absolute arm and hand targets. Episodes then pass through review, export and replay validation, with recorded simulator states retained for offline multi-view rendering. Figure 3 · Data collection pipeline. The operator wears a VR headset and gloves, with a controller mounted on each hand. Finger and wrist inputs are mapped to absolute joint targets, while VR rendering provides scene feedback. Episodes are recorded, reviewed, exported, validated and rendered offline. Full resolution ↗ 3,000 Replay-successful demonstrations 100 episodes per canonical stage, recorded at 20 Hz. State + action Restoration and replay Recorded state supports fidelity checks and open-loop trajectory validation. Multi-view Offline RGB rendering The same recorded interaction can be rendered from fixed base and wrist views. Six baselines reveal distinct limitations in stage execution, held-out-scene generalization and end-to-end task composition. title: Policy integration — DexArena
text: Docs / Policy integration Policy integration Map observations and model outputs into the registered joint-space interface without altering the task. The adapter boundary Read the environment’s action space, registered robot and camera profile. Convert image streams, proprioception and the canonical instruction into your model’s input schema. Convert the predicted action chunk to absolute joint targets in the environment’s exact joint order. Execute the chunk at 20 Hz; preserve success, termination and truncation signals. For a sequence, update the policy or instruction at stage transitions without resetting the simulator. Model coordinates are not controller coordinates The GR00T adapter uses relative arm offsets internally and converts them back to absolute targets for pd_joint_pos . An adapter must not pass relative offsets directly to that controller. Sharpa hand targets remain absolute. Contract Record with the policy Observation Image keys/order, resolution, state features, normalization and history. Action Joint order, absolute/relative conversion, units, chunk size and execution rate. Language Instruction version and stage-transition rule. Provenance Checkpoint, adapter revision, training data and environment source revision. Inspect algo/groot.py , train/train_groot.py and train/train_configs/groot_config.py for the implemented reference path. Other hands have their own spaces; the Sharpa 29/58-D layout is not universal. title: Parallel environments — DexArena
text: Docs / Parallel environments Parallel environments Scale evaluation by independent processes while preserving the single-environment native-scene contract. One scene evaluator per process The native-scene factory enforces one CPU-physics environment. It restores the registered robot, horizon, controller and camera profile and rejects incompatible overrides. The GR00T evaluation loop also requires num_eval_envs == 1 . Do not increase num_envs for this track Run separate processes for tasks, backgrounds or seed shards. Generic ManiSkill GPU-vectorized training capabilities do not imply vectorized support in this DexArena evaluation factory. Plan and inspect the 90-scene matrix python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90 python utils/scene_matrix.py preview --index 2 --out output/scene90/preview python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \ --out output/scene90/preview --shard 0 --shards 3 --resume The planner and previews check scene construction, not policy success. For policy sweeps, assign disjoint task/scene/seed tuples to workers, use separate output directories, and merge per-episode records only after checking duplicates and missing episodes. Record the same checkpoint, adapter, task revision and camera configuration for every shard. Aggregate by task rather than by worker so uneven shard sizes cannot change the score. Continue See Scene evaluation and aggregation rules .

title: Domain randomization — DexArena
text: Docs / Domain randomization Domain randomization Separate optional procedural variation from the fixed three-scene benchmark. Two different experiments The published generalization track uses three named native kitchen scenes with a frozen policy. Procedural texture, background and lighting randomization is an optional training or diagnostic tool; it is not a replacement for those three held-out scenes. Procedural randomization examples, not the three native leaderboard kitchens. Opt into a randomized builder from task.scene_builders import RandomizedTableSceneBuilder self.table_scene = RandomizedTableSceneBuilder( env=self, random_table_texture=True, random_background=True, random_lighting=True, ) self.table_scene.build() The builder’s defaults are inert. If table-height jitter is enabled, align object placement through table_top_offsets ; otherwise a visual change can also change the task geometry. Camera configuration remains task-controlled. Native scenes retain native geometry Native surfaces are aligned and checked within a 1 mm tabletop-height tolerance. Their authored collision geometry may differ. Record the background manifest rather than claiming that all background physics are identical. Continue For official paper-style comparisons, use the fixed native-scene matrix .

title: Teleoperation — DexArena
text: Docs / Teleoperation Teleoperation Collect wrist and finger motion, then review and replay the resulting demonstrations. Human motion to joint targets The collection setup uses a Quest 3 headset, MANUS Meta Gloves Pro and controllers mounted on the backs of the hands. Wrist tracking drives arm inverse kinematics; calibrated finger retargeting drives the selected hand. Select a formal collection target and match its environment ID and robot UID in the control and mirror processes. Calibrate the selected hand’s tracking and retargeting profile. Check the launch configuration with the available --dry-run mode before starting collection. Review the pending episode/video, then validate state restoration and open-loop replay before release. Ports and profiles The Sharpa bridge uses upstream port 2044 and downstream port 6668 . Wuji and XHand use their own configurations. Do not reuse a hand-specific SDK or joint map without checking the selected embodiment. The canonical registry contains 40 formal targets: 10 long-horizon environments and 30 stages. Older launch notes can contain retired counts; task/config/collection_targets.py takes precedence. Keep credentials out of shared artifacts SDK credentials belong in the local runtime setup, not in website documentation, logs or dataset exports. The site intentionally does not publish raw SDK command files. Address already in use If the SDK reports a ZeroMQ bind error, inspect the owning listener before starting another copy: ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )' Reuse the running bridge or close its owning terminal cleanly. Do not kill unrelated processes or change just one end of a paired connection. Continue Inspect Data & replay or the collection previews .

title: Embodiments — DexArena
text: Docs / Embodiments Embodiments A shared task family supports multiple end-effectors; published scores use the canonical Sharpa setup. Four supported end-effectors 01 Parallel-jaw gripper A gripper-based interface for cross-embodiment studies. 02 Sharpa Hand 22 hand joints per side; the canonical Panda-based data and paper evaluation setup. 03 Wuji Hand A separate robot/retargeting profile with its own action space. 04 XHand An additional dexterous-hand interface with embodiment-specific configuration. Supported is not scored The paper’s six-method leaderboard uses Panda + Sharpa. Multi-hand code support does not imply a full scored suite for every hand. Report an alternative embodiment as a separate study and document any task or controller differences. Sharpa control Action layout Single arm, 29-D Arm 7 → hand 22 Bimanual, 58-D Left arm 7 → right arm 7 → left hand 22 → right hand 22 Read other embodiments’ spaces from their registered agents. Do not pad or truncate to Sharpa dimensions without an explicit adapter. Match the selected robot UID, joint ordering, limits and calibration in both data collection and policy evaluation. Continue See Policy integration and Configurations .

title: Common issues — DexArena
text: Docs / Common issues Common issues Check the contract and process state before changing an evaluation configuration. Installation and assets Environment ID is not registered Run from the project checkout and import the task module before direct Gym creation. Check the canonical registry for the exact ID; aliases and retired curricula are not formal benchmark targets. Missing meshes or scene assets Confirm that the project’s robot, object and native-room assets are present. The website has no public source/dataset mirror yet; screenshots and the paper PDF are not a simulator installation package. GPU or renderer startup fails Check the local SAPIEN/ManiSkill environment and driver support independently of the policy. The native-scene contract specifies CPU physics; rendering still requires a working renderer. Evaluation and collection Action or state dimension mismatch Query the environment space. Sharpa single-arm and dual-arm layouts differ; task observation widths vary. Verify joint order, image keys, normalization and relative-to-absolute arm conversion. Factory rejects an override Use the registered horizon, robot, 256 × 256 policy camera profile, pd_joint_pos and one CPU environment. Avoid overriding these solely to bypass validation. Replay or native-scene validation fails Compare the task/source fingerprint, reset seed, background manifest and object placement. Restoring rigid state does not restore the solver’s transient contact cache; contact-dependent quantities are excluded from frame-restoration equality checks. SDK: Address already in use ss -ltnp '( sport = :2044 or sport = :6668 )' Check whether a previous Sharpa SDK bridge still owns either port, then reuse it or shut down its owning terminal cleanly. For another hand, inspect that hand’s configured ports. Continue Use the stub wiring test before a full policy run.

title: Leaderboard protocol — DexArena
text: Leaderboard Score protocol Three evaluation tracks, explicit aggregation and a reproducible evidence trail. Manuscript baselines, not a verified community leaderboard The current scores are the six paper baselines. Public submission intake, remote execution and independent verification are not yet available. Evaluation units 01 Stage execution 30 stages × 50 episodes in the training scene. Each stage starts from its own valid reset distribution. 02 Cross-scene 30 stages × 3 native scenes × 50 episodes. Freeze the policy; retain the background manifest for every run. 03 Long-horizon 10 sequences × 50 episodes. Reset once per episode, never between stages; measure final sequence completion. How scores are aggregated Stage and long-horizon averages weight tasks equally. For cross-scene results, average stage success within each scene first, then report the mean and standard deviation across the three scene averages. The ± value is scene variation, not a training-seed confidence interval. The original manuscript records ACT/DP stage seeds 50000–50049 and GR00T seeds 10001–10050. New comparison sweeps should use matched episode seeds across methods and record the manifest; do not imply the paper used identical seed ranges for every method. Keep task horizons and physical success predicates fixed. Persistent hold counters or latches are part of the task definition. π0.5 switches stage models for composition; GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. Reproduction package Identity Environment/task revision, robot UID, controller, horizon and seeds. Policy Checkpoint hash, adapter revision, training-data scope and observation preprocessing. Scenes Background IDs, camera profile and source/geometry manifests. Outcomes Per-episode success, steps, stage trace, logs, videos and aggregation script.
